title: Agentic AI & Automation Engineer
description: Guardrisk is the undisputed market leader in cell captive insurance and risk solutions. We are renowned for our innovative approach to cell captive structures and other alternative risk transfer solutions for our clients. Guardrisk offers clients custom designed cover and is registered in South Africa as an insurer for all statutory classes of non-life and life insurance business.Disclaimer As an applicant, please verify the legitimacy of this job advert on our company career page.Role PurposeWork directly with business users and Product Managers to understand and document business processes, identify high-value automation opportunities, and design, prototype and engineer production-ready workflows, automations and AI agents on Guardrisk’s governed platforms.What Makes This DifferentCombines workflow automation, software engineering and applied/agentic AIWorks directly in the business context to map processes, pain points, decisions, hand-offs and controlsIdentifies where to simplify, automate or augment work, rather than merely digitising an inefficient processRapidly prototypes automations and agents with users and learns through deploymentDesigns agentic workflows, orchestration, human-in-the-loop controls and exception handlingConnects business processes to systems, APIs, data, models and enterprise servicesBuilds reusable automation components, agent skills, tools and workflow patternsMakes sound design choices beyond one immediate use case, with reuse across Guardrisk in mindPartners with Technology on platform, integration, security and productionisationEstablishes the engineering practices, documentation and patterns needed to grow Guardrisk’s AI & Automation capabilitySupports adoption and measures whether deployed automations actually improve the underlying processExpected seniority: Energetic hands-on engineer with enough technical depth to engineer integrations, workflows and agents, but also enough business and product judgement to determine what should be automated, where AI adds value, where deterministic workflow is better, and where human judgement or control must remain.RequirementsMinimum QualificationsWe’re looking for someone who can operate across software, automation and AI rather than specialising in only one of them.Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.Strong software engineering experience in at least one modern programming language, ideally Python, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript or similar.Practical experience building workflow automations, system integrations or business process solutions.Experience designing and consuming REST APIs and integrating multiple systems or services.Hands-on experience building applications using large language models or generative AI APIs.Understanding of agentic concepts such as tool use, orchestration, retrieval, structured outputs, state and human-in-the-loop patterns.Experience taking solutions beyond prototypes into production or operational use.Ability to work directly with non-technical users to understand a business process and translate it into a technical solution.Strong engineering fundamentals, including source control, testing, documentation, security and maintainability.Ability to communicate technical trade-offs clearly to both business and technical stakeholders.Preferred QualificationsYou don’t need to have experience with every technology below. We’re particularly interested in people who have gone deep enough in this space to understand what works in production and what does not.Hands-on experience developing AI agents, multi-agent or agentic workflow solutions.Experience with agent frameworks, orchestration approaches or modern AI engineering toolchains.Experience with enterprise automation technologies such as Microsoft Power Automate, Power Platform, Azure Logic Apps or equivalent workflow/orchestration platforms.Experience with the Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 ecosystem, particularly where AI, automation and enterprise data intersect.Experience applying techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool/function calling, structured extraction and AI-assisted workflow orchestration.Experience with process discovery, process mapping, BPMN, Lean process improvement or similar approaches.Experience designing reusable automation platforms, components, libraries or engineering patterns rather than only delivering one-off solutions.Experience implementing evaluation, observability or monitoring for AI applications.Understanding of responsible AI, privacy, security and appropriate controls for deploying AI into business processes.Experience in financial services, insurance or another regulated environment.Evidence of being a builder and capability creator: someone comfortable starting with an ambiguous business problem, working with users, building something quickly and progressively turning it into a production-quality solution.Duties & ResponsibilitiesAbout The RoleWe’re building a practical Agentic AI and Automation capability at Guardrisk, and we’re looking for a hands-on engineer who wants to help shape it.This is not a role focused on producing AI demos or implementing technology in isolation. You will work directly with business teams to understand how work gets done, identify where processes can be simplified or automated, and turn those opportunities into working solutions.You’ll combine business process thinking, workflow automation, software engineering and applied AI to build everything from straightforward process automations and integrations to AI agents and agentic workflows.Just as importantly, you’ll help us create the capability itself: reusable components, patterns, engineering practices and skills that allow successful solutions to be applied across Guardrisk.Guardrisk’s Data & AI CoE is being designed around reusable capabilities and business-facing delivery, with AI and automation capacity forming part of that model. COE Org Structure The wider approach also envisages agents working across enterprise systems while retaining human decision-making where appropriate. CoE Ways of Working StandardWhat You Will DoWork directly with business users and Product Managers to understand, map and document end-to-end business processes.Identify manual work, bottlenecks, repetitive activities and hand-offs that can be simplified, automated or augmented using AI.Translate business problems into practical automation, workflow and agentic AI solutions.Rapidly prototype with users, test ideas in the real business context and turn successful prototypes into robust solutions.Design and build AI agents and agentic workflows that can reason over information, use tools, interact with enterprise systems and support business processes.Build traditional workflow automations where deterministic automation is a better fit than AI.Integrate solutions with enterprise systems, APIs, data and services.Design appropriate human-in-the-loop controls, approvals, exception handling and escalation paths.Develop reusable agent skills, tools, connectors, workflow components and automation patterns rather than solving every problem from scratch.Work with Technology, Architecture, Security and other teams to take solutions from prototype through to controlled production use.Build evaluation and monitoring into AI and automation solutions so that we understand whether they are working as intended and delivering value.Document solutions, patterns and lessons learned so that the capability becomes repeatable across Guardrisk.Help business and technical teams understand where agentic AI, conventional automation, integration or process redesign is the appropriate solution.Contribute to the standards and engineering practices that underpin Guardrisk’s emerging Agentic AI & Automation capability.CompetenciesCore OutputsDocumented business processes and automation opportunities.Production-ready workflow automations and integrations.AI agents and multi-step agentic workflows.Reusable agent skills, tools, connectors and automation components.Human-in-the-loop and exception-handling patterns.Working prototypes and MVPs.Process and solution designs.Evaluation, monitoring and operational controls.Deployment-ready code and technical documentation.Reusable engineering patterns and standards for Guardrisk.Knowledge transfer and practical enablement that grows internal automation capability.Enquiries title: Senior AI Engineer - LLM Adoption Department (LLMAD)
description: Job DescriptionBusiness OverviewRakuten Group, Inc. is a global leader in internet services that empower individuals, communities, businesses, and society. Founded in Tokyo in 1997 as an online marketplace, Rakuten has expanded to offer services in e-commerce, fintech, digital content, and communications to approximately 1.7 billion members around the world. The Rakuten Group has nearly 32,000 employees and operations in 30 countries and regions. For more information visit https://global.rakuten.com/corp/Department OverviewThe AI & Data Division (AIDD) creates powerful, customer-focused search, recommendation, data science, advertising, marketing, price, and inventory optimization solutions to a variety of businesses in the Rakuten group. Our goal is to drive innovation by developing new products and capabilities that deliver significant impact over longer timeframes using AI.The LLMAD team drives adoption of Rakuten AI and open-source LLMs hosted within our own environment. We're hiring AI Engineers who can be embedded directly inside business units to drive real adoption of in-house large language models in place of third-party alternatives.PositionPosition DetailsAs a Senior AI Engineer you will own a business unit engagement end to end. You sit inside their engineering team and build with them: designing the agent, selecting and evaluating the model, writing the prompts and tool-use logic, and getting it live in production on our own infrastructure.You are expected to operate independently - taking a vague business ask, turning it into a concrete and evaluable LLM task, and being accountable for it shipping. What you build also becomes reusable: the cookbooks, recipes, and reference implementations the rest of the team and other business units start from.・Own a business unit engagement end to end - embed in their engineering team, design the agent (task decomposition, tool and function calling, multi-step orchestration, state, retrieval, guardrails), and write production code in their codebase.・Take agents from prototype to production and own what that requires: latency, cost, failure modes, and monitoring - including the judgment to say early when an agent is the wrong answer and a prompt, a fine-tune, or plain software is not.・Select the right in-house or open-source model for each task and prove it with task-level evaluation rather than benchmark scores, building the eval sets and harnesses together with the business unit.・Run migrations from third-party APIs to our in-house models - parity testing, prompt porting, staged cutover - and feed the gaps you find back to our model and platform teams.・Own prompt and context engineering as a discipline: structured output, tool schemas, retrieval strategy, and caching, versioned and measured against evals; debug quality problems down to whether the fault is the prompt, the retrieval, the model, or the data.・Turn the work into cookbooks, recipes, and reference implementations other business units can lift directly, and raise the bar around you through code review, mentorship, and hands-on enablement for business unit engineers.This role sits close to the product rather than close to the model:・You will not be training or fine-tuning foundation models - that sits with our model research and training teams.・You will not be building the LLM platform itself - that sits with our platform engineering teams.・You will be embedded in a business unit, writing agent and integration code inside their product, and accountable for it shipping on our models.Mandatory Qualifications・Over 6 years of professional software engineering experience, with recent hands-on focus on building LLM applications. You are shipping this work today.・Proven agentic engineering experience: you have built, shipped, evaluated, and debugged agents in production - tool and function calling, multi-step orchestration, and the failure modes that come with them.・Prompt and context engineering as a discipline: structured outputs, systematic iteration against evals, and versioning.・Practical model knowledge: the strengths and weaknesses of open-weight and commercial models, when to fine-tune versus prompt versus retrieve, and the cost and latency trade-offs of each.・Solid production fundamentals: APIs, backend services, testing, observability, and experience with self-hosted or cloud inference (e.g., vLLM).・Able to work embedded in someone else's engineering team, communicate directly with business stakeholders, and operate with the ambiguity of a function that is still being defined.・Writes things down - docs, examples, and recipes other engineers can actually use.Desired Qualifications・Japanese language ability - a significant plus. Our business unit teams work in Japanese day to day, and being able to work in the language directly makes the embedded model far more effective.・Experience migrating production applications from third-party LLM APIs to self-hosted or open-weight models.・Retrieval-augmented generation at production scale.・Exposure to fine-tuning or post-training, enough to know when to reach for it.・Experience delivering with distributed teams in Japan or Asia.#engineer #applicationsengineer #aianddatadiv Show more Show less
